data.title: Three Days to Go: Four Core Highlights of the 2026 iCAUR International User Summit
data.description:
Key points:
  • With just three days to go, the 2026 iCAUR International User Summit will feature four core highlights under the theme "Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours": brand launch, user co-creation, test-drive experience and ecosystem engagement.
  • The iCAUR V25 will make its official debut at the summit, joining the V23 and V27 to further enrich the V Series lineup.
  • The first iCAUR Customization Festival will kick off, featuring 20 customized vehicles and the launch of “User-centric Experience” global user ecosystem.
  • The V Series Test-Drive Camp, Ecosystem Showroom, AiMOGA robot, Robotaxi products and technologies will deliver a multi-dimensional immersive experience.

WUHU, China, Oct. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The 2026 iCAUR International User Summit will run from October 19 to 23. With just three days to go before the opening, Chery Group’s iCAUR has unveiled a slate of highlights under the theme "Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours," including the world premiere of the V25, the first iCAUR Customization Festival, the V Series Test-Drive Camp, and interactive tours of the Ecosystem Showroom. Global media and attendees will experience iCAUR's Future-Classic Design philosophy firsthand, see how V Series vehicles go beyond mobility to enrich everyday life, and gain deeper insights into the open ecosystem co-created by iCAUR and its global user community.

【Poster for 2026 iCAUR International User Summit】

Highlight One: World Premiere of the V25, A New Addition to the V Series Family

The iCAUR Global Brand & V25 World Premiere will be officially held on October 19. Positioned as an all-way SUV, the iCAUR V25 will make its global debut at the event, expanding the V Series lineup alongside the V23 and V27.

Built for both daily city commutes and outdoor adventures, the V25 embodies iCAUR’s latest Future-Classic Design language through its iconic boxy silhouette, near 1:1 width-to-height ratio and signature round headlamps. Backed by the i-AWD (Intelligent All-wheel Drive) and Golden REEV (Range-extended Electric Vehicle) systems, the vehicle confidently handles diverse road conditions, enabling seamless transitions between urban travel, long-distance trips and outdoor exploration. Boasting more than 20 ecosystem interfaces, a 1.8-tonne towing capacity and 6kW external discharge capability, it supports lifestyle scenarios such as camping, cycling and photography. Three official customized vehicles based on the V23, V25 and V27 will also be showcased together on site, demonstrating the wide-ranging lifestyle integration possibilities of the V Series.

【V25】

Highlight Two: Inaugural Customization Festival, Putting User Creativity on Stage

Beyond official customized vehicles, genuine user creativity will take the spotlight at the first iCAUR Customization Festival. Built around “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours”, the venue is split into three experience zones: Custom Car, Urban Lifestyle and Outdoor Lifestyle. A collection of customized vehicles from across the globe spans off-road, camping and urban commuting use cases, visually demonstrating the V Series’ potential for expansion in styling, functionality and ecosystem connectivity. Attendees may cast votes for their favourite builds and winners may receive limited-edition stickers. Within the Custom Car zone, participants can try modular installations under professional guidance, learn how vehicle interfaces power various functions, and exchange ideas with fellow enthusiasts worldwide. The Urban and Outdoor Lifestyle Experience Zones host interactive activities including coffee tastings, graffiti creation and physical challenges, helping users discover new connections between vehicles and daily life aligned with personal interests.

On the occasion, the brand will launch the “User-centric Experience” global user ecosystem.

Supported by four foundational pillars — official iCAUR customized vehicles, the iCAUR Customization Festival, the iCAUR APP and iCAUR Club Connect — this framework embeds user experience and creativity into product and ecosystem development. Using vehicles as its medium, the iCAUR Customization Festival establishes a platform for global vehicle owners, customization enthusiasts and the brand to communicate and co-create, turning “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours” into an ongoing collective journey where users participate in defining what constitutes a classic.

【Past iCAUR Customized Vehicle】

Highlight Three: V Series Test-Drive Camp — Hands-on Vehicle Trials

Product experience moves beyond static displays to real-world driving scenarios at the V Series Test-Drive Camp. Both the V25 and the V27 will be available for test drives across urban roads, undulating terrain and complex outdoor surfaces, allowing media and users to get behind the wheel and experience the two boxy SUVs firsthand, evaluating power response, handling stability, off-road capability and ride comfort.

A core focus of the experience is how the vehicles maintain stability and handle changing terrain. The all-new Swift Agile Handling Platform engineered by iCAUR features a native NEV (New Energy Vehicle) architecture. Built on a modular building-block concept, it enables flexible integration of powertrain, chassis, intelligent systems and cabin space to address differentiated mobility needs. The platform-dedicated i-AWD system dynamically adapts drive configurations to road conditions and apportions wheel torque with millisecond responsiveness, elevating off-road capability and handling performance on slippery surfaces, gravel tracks and steep gradients. Golden REEV achieves high-efficiency fuel-to-electricity conversion with a thermal efficiency of 44.5%. Behind the wheel across varied terrain, attendees will directly experience how i-AWD optimises power distribution and driving stability, while appreciating the near-BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle) driving refinement delivered by Golden REEV technology.

Highlight Four: Ecosystem Showroom and New Product Launch by AiMOGA Robot, Unlocking New Technological Potential

Beyond vehicles themselves, the iCAUR Ecosystem Showroom centres its design on “Classic Never Fades”. It houses three zones — Lifestyle Lab, Time Corridor and Creation Hub — crafting an immersive experience that stretches from design inspiration to real-world living scenarios. The pavilion features V23 and V27 customized vehicles, V27 design sketches, user creations and ecosystem product exhibits. Visitors can trace a vehicle’s journey from design sketch to finished product, and see how it adapts to diverse lifestyle scenarios via interfaces, accessories and user imagination. Zones including the Life Lab and Time Corridor respectively explore urban living, sensory experience and personalised creation, showcasing iCAUR’s design philosophy and how users can leave their own mark on their vehicles through customization and co-creation. Attendees can draw inspiration from diverse customization concepts and witness how Future-Classic Design continues to evolve through user innovation.

During the summit, the brand will also unveil new products and technologies related to the AiMOGA robot and Robotaxi, offering global users another perspective to explore the application of intelligent technologies.

In three days’ time, “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours” will come to life — from a single new vehicle to a thriving user community; from individual customizations to a continuously connected global ecosystem. Through these four core highlights, this year’s iCAUR International User Summit turns “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours” from a brand statement into a tangible, visible and inclusive shared practice.

Serena Wang

data.title: HDFC Bank Q2 Results: Net profit rises 5% to Rs.19,610 crore, NII jumps 10% in last quarter under outgoing CEO Jagdishan
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- HDFC Bank, India's largest private sector lender, on Saturday announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 5.2% year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone net profit to Rs.19,609.96 crore.

The bank's profit after tax (PAT) was Rs.18,641.28 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. On a sequential basis, net profit grew 2.83% from Rs.19,069.72 crore in the June 2026 quarter.

Net interest income (NII), which represents the difference between interest earned and interest expended, increased 9.72% YoY to Rs.34,619.18 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.31,551.50 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total interest earned during the quarter stood at Rs.83,426.60 crore.

The bank's net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.16% on total assets and 3.32% on interest-earning assets.

The quarter is also significant as it is expected to be the final earnings report under managing director and chief executive officer Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ends on October 26. Anup Bagchi is set to replace him.

HDFC Bank Q2 Results: Asset quality improves

HDFC Bank reported an improvement in its gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio, which declined to 1.11% of gross advances as of September 30, 2026. This compared with 1.17% in the preceding quarter and 1.24% in the year-ago period.

The net non-performing asset (NNPA) ratio remained stable at 0.37%, indicating that the bank's reported net bad-loan ratio was unchanged.

data.title: AI rapidly improving, could vastly boost US GDP, Anthropic's Clark tells policymakers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Internal model forecasts US GDP could reach $44 trillion by 2030 under certain conditions
  • Clark says window to impose AI safeguards is shrinking
  • Clark urged international cooperation on regulation

By David Lawder

Rapidly improving artificial intelligence capabilities will bring far faster change across all fields, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday, with one of the company's internal models forecasting that under certain conditions it could increase US economic output by almost 50% by 2030.

Clark, speaking at IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, said that international cooperation was needed to erect "unusual and serious rules" for the transformative technology, and there was a shrinking window for policymakers to act.

Clark said that the estimated potential US GDP of $44 trillion, which compares to the current level of just over $30 trillion, "sounds very outlandish, I know." But he added that AI was vastly increasing scientific discovery.

He said the forecast assumed "the technology continuing to get better. And if GDP were to grow this much, then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need to have been created to power such a major economic expansion".

Clark's remarks come as the company prepares for an initial public offering expected in November that could value the firm at up to $2 trillion.

HUMANS IN CONTROL, FOR NOW

Clark issued a wake-up call to policymakers about the speed of AI development, saying there was growing evidence of a "singularity" where AI development outpaces human control.

"We should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI but science as a whole will speed up, and this will feel confusing and disorienting, and will bring with it great wealth and potentially great peril," he said in a lecture to hundreds of government and finance officials.

AI was a major topic at the IMF and World Bank meetings, as both a source of growth offsetting high energy prices and a potential threat to stability if it falls short of its promise as a productivity game-changer and stock valuations crash.

Officials also expressed worries about AI destroying certain jobs and leaving some countries behind.

But Clark, a former journalist who serves as Anthropic's "head of public benefit," painted a picture of a rosy future where AI was a force multiplier for scientific discovery, solving mathematical, engineering and biological problems, including new drug discovery, as human researchers are supplemented by hundreds or thousands of AI assistants.

More countries can participate in the AI revolution by helping to build the data center computing capacity needed to power AI, he said.

STRICTEST CONTROLS ON BIOLOGICAL RESEARCH

Clark cautioned that global leaders need to understand how powerful AI will become and make urgent choices about how to regulate the technology.

"Being able to use AI for science opens us up to the misuses of science as well, biological and cyber weapons and things we cannot yet imagine, and we have many choices to make," he said.

Biological research, where AI has already created new viruses, is an area "where we want the strictest human oversight and transparency to maintain safety."

Despite some recent high-profile incidents where rogue AI systems have escaped testing environments and hacked websites and databases, he said AI was still under human control. But the window to impose safeguards was shrinking as AI became more capable and was now "a small number of years."

Clark also acknowledged that AI was causing job losses in some fields with "high AI exposure" such as call centers and customer service personnel. But for other fields, such as scientific research, he said AI was enhancing employment and a major unknown was its potential to create jobs in completely new industries.

data.title: It was another great week for the average stock as market leadership shifts away from tech
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis and Isabel Wang

The S&P 500's tech sector just had its worst week in a year and a half, while an equal-weighted version of the index cemented a second-straight weekly advance

The average stock in the S&P 500 just had a decent week, although a slump in tech masked that shine at the index level.

Investors aren't bailing on the stock market, despite an ugly selloff in technology names this week that helped to saddle the S&P 500 with its worst weekly showing in months.

The S&P 500 SPX lost almost 2% even as the majority of the index's stocks actually advanced on the week. Seventy percent of stocks in the index posted weekly gains while 30% fell, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That helped the equal-weighted version of the index XX:SP500EW cement a second-straight week in the green. When the dust had settled, the S&P 500 had cemented its worst weekly showing since June, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Following a powerful but narrow tech-led rally, this week's action offered the latest indication that market leadership is shifting once again. While tech stocks and some industrial names tied to the artificial-intelligence build-out slumped this week, the average stock in the increasingly top-heavy S&P 500 made it through a difficult week largely unscathed.

Defensive and interest-rate-sensitive areas of the market moved sharply higher this week, as stocks that had lagged over the past two months shot upward. This has given hard-hit corners of the market a chance to shine.

"Given that there's growing concerns around the AI trade and volatility in spending these companies are doing, it just makes sense for investors to broaden their view a little bit and look for other opportunities," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial, in a phone interview Friday. "Now money is rotating out of tech into areas that had been really depressed."

Certainly, it helped that interest rates in the bond market saw a big pullback from recent highs, providing some broad relief to stocks.

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP, a popular exchange-traded fund that equally weights stocks in the index, rose 0.5% this week. By contrast, the S&P 500 saw its biggest weekly percentage drop since June 26.

The big drag on the S&P 500 is its largest sector, information technology XX:SP500.45, which was pummeled this week with a 6.4% drop. That left the tech sector with its biggest weekly loss since April 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Meanwhile, seven of the S&P 500's 11 sectors saw weekly gains, FactSet data showed.

"Nobody really wants to be out of the market," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, in a phone interview Friday. "If people were really genuinely concerned about the stock market right now, they'd be selling and not rushing to buy something else."

Among traditionally defensive areas of the stock market, the S&P 500's consumer-staples sector XX:SP500.30 surged 5% this week. Another defensive area, healthcare XX:SP500.35, had a big climb of 3.4%, while rate-sensitive stocks like materials XX:SP500.15 and utilities XX:SP500.55 also jumped sharply.

The decline in interest rates this week was significant, as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield BX:TMUBMUSD10Y "backed off pretty dramatically," Saglimbene noted. The 10-year Treasury rate fell this week to 5.097% on Friday, locking in its biggest weekly pullback since February, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Bond yields move inversely with bond prices.

That's down from the 10-year rate's recent high of 5.31% on Oct. 5. Yields on 10-year and 30-year BX:TMUBMUSD30Y Treasurys have risen to their highest levels in decades this year.

"With some improvement on the rates front, people do feel it's safe to move some money back into rate-sensitive sectors like financials XX:SP500.40, industrials XX:SP500.20 and real estate XX:SP500.60," Sosnick said.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury dropped Thursday despite a hot reading on wholesale inflation from the producer-price index that same day, partly because "there was a bit of a flight-to-safety trade on top of it surrounding CoreWeave," Sosnick said - referring to the neocloud company (CRWV) whose stock tumbled this week on worries over its AI-related borrowing.

Tech had been the stock market's "safety trade," rising when Treasury yields were spiking in September, as investors appeared confident about the AI trade continuing to power higher despite higher rates, said Keith Lerner, CIO at Truist Wealth, by phone on Friday.

Last month, tech looked like "the only place in town," he noted, "while all these other areas were beat up." Now, it appears the tide has turned.

"Instead of a broad-based selloff across the board, you're just seeing a rotation from tech to everything else," Lerner said. "A rotational market is better than when money is broadly leaving the market."

-Christine Idzelis -Isabel Wang

data.title: Hari, shankar, mahadev: the enigma behind skyexchange
data.description:
Syndicate Kingpin Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal (HST) owner of Skyexchange. ED says HST’s SkyExchange and the Mahadev App were run in Partnership, “A constituent part of the same criminal enterprise."

HST Wins Curbs On The Press In Delhi's Lower Courts

But ED’s Raipur Files Tell Another Story

He carries two Gods in his name. Hari is Vishnu, the preserver. Shankar is Shiva, whom devotees also call Mahadev.

In the files of India's Enforcement Directorate (ED), the aganecy probing money laundering, the third name follows close behind.

The ED says Hari Shankar Tibrewal’s betting platform, SkyExchange, was “co-owned and co-promoted in partnership with” the promoters of Mahadev Online Book. That made it, in the agency’s words, “a constituent part of the same criminal enterprise.” Mahadev is the app at the centre of one of India’s largest betting investigations, which the ED estimates generated Rs 75,000–80,000 crore.

To the men around him, he was simply “Hari Bhai.” In an astrologer’s WhatsApp chat recovered from a jailed businessman’s phone, he appears only as three letters and a date of birth: “HST.” In the ED’s charge sheet he is Accused No. 24. The ED twice summoned him to Raipur, and twice the record reads: “Did not appear.”

And in a Delhi courtroom on September 23, he won a court order restricting what the press may call him.

THE ENIGMA

Delhi courts have restrained some news outlets from branding him with labels. But EDs own documents, which no injunction covers, describe in detail the man they call “HST”

A judge confirmed interim injunctions in HST's civil defamation suit. The judge found that publications calling him a “Hawala Trader”, a “key figure in stock market manipulation scheme” and a “shadowy titan in a financial underworld” prima facie attributed criminality to a man no court has convicted. The court also found that later articles using words such as “absconding”, “farar” and “fugitive from Indian justice” fell within the category of material it had already ordered taken down.

To Tibrewal, it was vindication. To a growing number of newsrooms, it has become something else: a legal tool that hangs over any outlet trying to write about him.

“Those accused of white-collar crimes are using the law to gag the media. It gives them a cover, and it intimidates the very press that can put pressure on the system protecting them,” a lawyer of a leading Delhi news agency told BW.

In case of HST, the order does not stop the story being told. The court did not impose a blanket ban on reporting about Tibrewal. As reported, it distinguished between branding a man a criminal and fairly reporting what investigators and courts have said, and it left the second untouched. That matters, because the investigators have said a great deal.

THE MAN IN THE FILES

The ED has filed two documents this year in the Mahadev betting-app case. The first is Provisional Attachment Order No. 16/2026 of June 5. The second is a 375-page supplementary prosecution complaint filed in Raipur in September. Neither treats Tibrewal as a peripheral figure.

The attachment order calls him “HST.”

It says the betting platform SkyExchange was “operated by Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal from Kolkata” and was “co-owned and co-promoted in partnership with” Mahadev’s promoters Sourabh Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal, making it “a constituent part of the same criminal enterprise.” The ED’s first hook on him was a 2020 FIR at Kolkata’s Burtolla police station.

The charge sheet names him Accused No. 24 and describes him as a man who “hails from Kolkata but currently residing in Dubai.”

In its section on EaseMyTrip co-founder Nishant Pitti, it uses a phrase no Delhi court has struck from an ED filing: “Syndicate Kingpin Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal (owner of Skyexchange).”

SUMMONED TWICE, APPEARED NEVER

Both documents record the same thing. The ED summoned Tibrewal under Section 50 of the PMLA on April 22, 2024 and again on April 25, 2024. Both times the entry reads: “Did not appear.”

He has not appeared since, according to the documents. Since then the agency has frozen Rs 580.78 crore of securities it says he beneficially owns, named him as an accused, attached Rs 940 crore of assets linked to an alleged business partner, and filed a sixth supplementary charge sheet with his name on almost every page that matters. He is now understood to be in London, sources say.

Rs 22 CR A Week

The ED’s estimate of the SkyExchange business is built on one ledger, seized from Prashant Bagri, who the charge sheet says has been “an employee of Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal since 2017.” The ledger listed the platform’s super-admins and a single week’s earnings: about Rs 22 crore. Extrapolated from 2016, the ED puts SkyExchange’s proceeds at Rs 11,000–12,000 crore, alongside an estimated Rs 75,000–80,000 crore for Mahadev.

It says Mahadev’s promoters held admin IDs on SkyExchange and could create “master and Super IDs.” In the ED’s words, they were partners running “both the said Applications parallelly with same modus-operandi.”

The world around that money is described in the same charge sheet: - A Rs 200-crore wedding for Chandrakar in Ras Al Khaimah, paid in cash. - Private jets from Nagpur, and Rs 112 crore sent by hawala to an event company. - Call centres run out of villas in Dubai’s Al Barsha district, each housing 50 to 70 people.

THE 30% CASHBACK

The most damaging passages describe how, according to the ED, betting money became stock-market money.

Tibrewal, the charge sheet says, “invests huge amount of funds in Indian Listed entities after making the deals with the Promoters of the said Indian entities and in return, the Indian entities have to pay cashback (in the range of 30% to 40% of total investment) in cash.” The cash was collected in Delhi, it says, by his associate Gagan Gupta (“Gagan Bhai”) and Gupta’s men.

ED Names the Deals: -

Salasar Techno Engineering. Investments of Rs 81.9 crore in 2022 and about Rs 130 crore in 2024. The ED says the promoters returned about Rs 25 crore and Rs 40 crore in cash “in cash and Hawala Channels.” - Tiger Logistics. A fixer told the ED he collected Rs 5–6 crore in cash from the promoter as “cashback (30% of total investment)” and handed it to Gupta’s associates.

EaseMyTrip. Tibrewal’s front fund, AG Dynamic Funds, allegedly bought 1.51 crore shares worth Rs 59.6 crore after a “pre-arranged” deal with Pitti. Pitti has called the allegations “completely baseless.” -

Toyam Sports. A seized tracking sheet lists shareholdings against the name “Hari.” - Vikas Garg’s companies. Rs 765.77 crore allegedly went into the companies of Garg, the Delhi businessman, which used it to buy the US software firm Ebix.

A WARDROBE OF FUNDS

Instead of simply hoarding illegal cash, Tibrewal structured a system to inject betting proceeds into the Indian equity market using the Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) route. This route was actively leveraged to corner stakes in small, mid-cap, and SME-listed companies.

The ED attributes a long list of offshore vehicles to him: - Funds: AG Dynamic Funds, Forbes EMF, Coeus Global, Ebisu Global, Oyster Bay, Plutus, and Tano Investment Opportunities in Mauritius. - Dubai companies: Zenith Multi Trading DMCC, Plus Commodities, Ecotek General Trading, Caterfiled Global and JE Impex.

The ED Also Details the Disguises:

Ecotek. A witness told the ED that the recorded 100% owner was “just benamidar of Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal.”

Zenith. The registered email address, the ED says, belongs to Tibrewal. - Tano. The attachment order says he “changed the beneficial ownership… mid-investigation, immediately upon issuance of summons.”

When the ED asked Tano to identify its owner, it named four entities, all of which ignored summons. Then Mauritius’s Financial Services Commission wrote to SEBI identifying Tibrewal as the beneficial owner. The ED notes the letter came “post every attempt… to show that Hari Shankar Tibrewal is not the beneficial owner.”

“HARI BHAI” AT THE TAJ

The charge sheet also places HST at the centre of the Ebix takeover. According to two witnesses, Tibrewal was at meetings at the Taj hotel in London in mid-2024 with Vikas Garg. Shown his photograph, he was identified as “the main investor on behalf of all the entities.” Travel records, the ED says, back their accounts.

Sunil Bhandari, another accused, told investigators that Garg and Tibrewal “are partners and involved in price rigging of certain listed entities by using the funds generated at Skyexchange.”

Garg, now the only one of 14 arrested accused still in custody, at first told the ED he knew Tibrewal was in illegal betting. After his arrest he said he did not know him. The ED says Garg’s seized iPhone holds a February 2025 call in which he discusses money with Gagan Gupta and refers to “Hari, Hari Bhai.” It also holds a WhatsApp exchange with an astrologer about “HST,” giving a date of birth the ED says matches Tibrewal’s.

The KOLKATA NETWORK

Before Dubai, there was Kolkata.

The ED's attachment order says SkyExchange was "operated by Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal from Kolkata." The trail starts in the city too. The first case linked to him was an FIR registered on 24 September 2020 at Burtolla police station, in the heart of north Kolkata's old trading district. Kolkata Police filed a charge sheet in that case on 29 October 2024 under the IPC and the West Bengal Gambling and Prize Competitions Act. (Charge sheet, Burtolla FIR details; attachment order.)

The ED says the money ran through the city's shell-company economy:

Cash into bank entries. Kolkata entry operator Amit Saraogi (A-37) told the ED he provided "bank entries to the tune of Rs. 150 crore against cash" to Ability Games Ltd, Swamim Vanijya and Nischaya Trading. The charge sheet describes those as companies "of Mr Hari Shankar Tibrewal." He said he did this on the instructions of Sanjeev Bera, whom the ED describes as Tibrewal's employee. (Chargesheet, Saraogi statement.)

Another Rs 200 crore in entries went to companies of Suraj Chokhani (A-25), whom the ED describes as the man who "manages the operations of Indian entities of Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal." (Charge sheet, Saraogi statement; Gagan Gupta call records.)

The shell factory. Saraogi's companies used dummy directors. Reports of his statement say he ran 40–50 shells, paid the dummy directors Rs 1,500–3,000 a month, and earned 1.25% commission. (Charge sheet; edatabook, May 2024.)

The phone records. Call records of Gagan Gupta show him in "regular touch" with Tibrewal, Saraogi, Chokhani and Bagri. The ED calls this the inner circle around SkyExchange. (Chargesheet.)

The pipeline. Again and again, the charge sheet says money that reached Vikas Garg's companies and Sunil Bhandari's firms came originally "from Kolkata based shell entities," arranged by Tibrewal.

A casino deal. Ability Games Ltd (A-26), which the charge sheet lists among Tibrewal's companies, signed an agreement to buy the Nepal casino business of the listed gaming company Delta Corp, according to reports of the ED's findings. (edatabook/Free Press Journal; check against Delta Corp's stock-exchange filing before use.)

THE QUESTIONS INDIA HASN'T ANSWERED

The ED says Tibrewal has twice declined to appear before it. It calls him the owner of a Rs 11,000-crore betting platform and lists him as an accused in a money-laundering prosecution. That raises questions the agency has not publicly answered.

Fugitive Economic Offenders Act. The 2018 Act lets the ED ask a special court to declare someone a fugitive economic offender if a warrant has been issued, the offence exceeds Rs 100 crore, and the person has left India and refuses to return. Has the ED moved such an application against Tibrewal?

Warrant. Is there a non-bailable warrant against him? The new charge sheet seeks warrants against Gagan Gupta and two others, but does not list Tibrewal among them. Why?

Extradition. India has an extradition treaty with the UAE, and has used it in other cases. Has India sought his extradition, or a Red Notice? Ministry of External Affairs and ED must look

If he is in the UK, India–UK extradition proceedings are slow; see the Nirav Modi and Vijay Mallya cases. Is this the reason that those wanted in cases like HST shift to London?

Until those questions are answered, the record shows a contrast. The man the ED calls a “Syndicate Kingpin” has not answered its summons in Raipur, while in Delhi he has won injunctions against outlets that wrote about him.

An “Escapee” from India who's yet to be delcared an Absconder. Delhi's lower court's need to take the ED cases and summons into account.

Tibrewal has denied any role in the Mahadev app or SkyExchange and rejects the allegations against him. None of the charges has been tested at trial. But he remains outside India and does not appear before ED.

data.title: IDBI Bank Sale: Government Says Employee Concerns Addressed
data.description:
The Finance Ministry says existing employees’ service conditions and pension benefits will be protected under the proposed Rs 52,878 crore stake sale

The government has said legitimate concerns of IDBI Bank employees and other stakeholders have been addressed through provisions in the share purchase agreement for the lender’s proposed privatisation, even as employee associations continue to oppose the transaction.

Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary told the Lok Sabha that safeguards for existing employees and other stakeholders had been incorporated into the agreement. The response came amid questions about the potential impact of the proposed sale on employees and whether the government had consulted bank staff and their representatives.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to 10955230 Canada Inc., a subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings, for Rs 52,878 crore. The transaction involves the government selling its 30.48 per cent holding and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) divesting its 30.24 per cent stake. Following the sale, the government will retain 15 per cent and LIC 19 per cent.

The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has separately stated that existing employees’ service conditions will remain protected and pension benefits will be safeguarded through a dedicated pension fund.

However, the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees has disputed claims that employee representatives were consulted during the process. The forum has called for the transaction to be reviewed, citing concerns over employee safeguards, the bank’s valuation and the implications of transferring control to a foreign investor. It has also sought greater transparency over the valuation methodology and transaction terms.

The proposed disinvestment process began with the publication of a preliminary information memorandum on 7 October 2022, inviting expressions of interest from potential bidders. The transaction remains subject to the required regulatory approvals and completion procedures.

The competing positions highlight the importance of employee protections and consultation as the government advances the strategic sale of the bank.

data.title: India Excludes Sugar-Based Ethanol From 2026-27 Tender
data.description:
State-run oil marketing companies seek 11 billion litres of ethanol from grain-based feedstocks, while reducing the price incentive for corn-based supplies

India has set sugar diversion for ethanol production at zero for the 2026-27 supply year, excluding sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from the latest procurement tender. The move comes amid concerns over domestic sugar availability, lower production prospects and rising prices.

The tender, issued on 16 October by Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, invites bids for 11 billion litres of ethanol for the supply year beginning in November. Suppliers can offer ethanol made from corn, broken rice and surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India.

The decision signals a shift in feedstock procurement as India seeks to balance its ethanol-blending programme with the need to maintain domestic sugar supplies.

Grain-Based Ethanol Takes Priority

The tender states that the government has directed oil marketing companies to reduce sugar diversion for ethanol production to zero for the 2026-27 supply year. Accordingly, the companies have not invited bids for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar or sugar syrup, and B-heavy molasses.

India has used surplus sugar and sugarcane-based feedstocks to support ethanol production and reduce dependence on imported crude oil. The latest tender instead directs procurement towards grain-based alternatives, including corn and rice.

The change comes as poor rainfall in key sugar-producing states, including Maharashtra and Karnataka, has raised concerns about sugar output. Lower production prospects have added pressure to domestic supplies and prices.

Corn Ethanol Incentive Falls

The tender also reduces the incentive for corn-based ethanol to Rs 2.79 per litre from Rs 5.79 per litre. The procurement price consequently falls to Rs 68.86 per litre from Rs 71.86 per litre.

The lower incentive changes the commercial terms for suppliers that use corn as a feedstock. The impact on procurement and production will depend on the economics of grain availability, processing costs and the prices offered under the tender.

The procurement framework allows suppliers to use surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India, alongside corn and broken rice. This provides alternative feedstocks as sugar-based ethanol remains outside the latest tender.

India has expanded ethanol blending to reduce crude oil imports and curb pollution. The government made the E20 blend, which contains 20 per cent ethanol, the nationwide mandatory standard earlier in 2026. However, some motorists have raised concerns about its compatibility with older vehicles.

data.title: HDFC Bank Q2 Profit Rises 5%, Misses Estimates At Rs 19,510 Cr
data.description:
India’s largest private-sector lender reports a year-on-year increase in second-quarter profit, while net interest income falls short of forecasts and provisions rise amid improving asset quality

HDFC Bank reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the second quarter of the 2026–27 financial year, but the result fell short of market expectations.

The lender’s net profit was below the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 19,727 crore. It had reported a profit of Rs 18,641 crore in the corresponding quarter a year earlier.

The results, announced on Saturday, 17 October, reflect continued growth in the bank’s core lending business, alongside higher provisioning expenses and weaker-than-expected operating performance.

Net Interest Income Misses Forecast

Net interest income (NII), which measures the difference between interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits, rose 10 per cent year-on-year to Rs 34,619 crore.

However, the figure was below the estimated Rs 34,991 crore.

Operating profit increased 5.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 29,483 crore, compared with Rs 27,923 crore in the year-ago period. The result also missed the market estimate of Rs 29,868 crore.

The bank’s net interest margin (NIM), based on total assets, stood at 3.16 per cent.

Provisions Increase, Asset Quality Improves

HDFC Bank’s provisions rose to Rs 3,574 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 3,059 crore in the preceding quarter and Rs 3,500 crore a year earlier.

Despite the increase in provisions, asset quality improved sequentially.

The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio declined to 1.11 per cent from 1.17 per cent in the previous quarter, beating the estimated 1.14 per cent. The net NPA ratio also fell to 0.37 per cent from 0.41 per cent, against an estimate of 0.39 per cent.

The improvement in these ratios indicates a lower proportion of stressed loans relative to the bank’s advances, although provisioning costs remain an important factor for earnings.

Loan Growth Remains Strong

HDFC Bank continued to expand its lending portfolio during the quarter.

Average advances under management increased 14.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31.87 lakh crore. Gross advances at the end of September stood at Rs 32.20 lakh crore, representing growth of 16.3 per cent from a year earlier.

Retail loans grew 11.7 per cent year-on-year, while lending to small and mid-market enterprises increased 23.5 per cent.

On the funding side, average deposits rose 16.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31.66 lakh crore. Average current account and savings account (CASA) deposits increased 10.7 per cent to Rs 9.71 lakh crore.

The results highlight the bank’s continued loan and deposit growth, even as its profitability metrics remain below market expectations in some key areas.

data.title: Centre Reaffirms Right To Dilute Stake In IDBI Bank, Cites 2018 Court Ruling
data.description:
The government has cited the 2018 judgment, which held that parliamentary statements could not override enacted legislation, to clarify its authority to reduce or divest its shareholding in IDBI Bank amid ongoing strategic disinvestment efforts

The Centre has reiterated its legal authority to dilute or divest its shareholding in IDBI Bank, citing a 2018 Delhi High Court judgment that held the government could not be prevented from reducing its stake on the basis of statements made during parliamentary debates.

In a clarification issued on 17 October, the government said an amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of its stake in IDBI was moved during discussions on the Union Budget in 2003 and the parliamentary debate on the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003. However, the amendment was ultimately rejected and did not form part of the enacted legislation.

The government’s statement comes amid media reports and commentary on the legislative developments surrounding its shareholding in the bank.

Delhi High Court ruling on government’s shareholding

The Centre referred to the judgment in All India IDBI Officers’ Association v. Union of India & Others, delivered by the Delhi High Court on 17 December 2018. The court dismissed the writ petition and held that statements made in Parliament during legislative debates could not override the law ultimately enacted.

The court observed that the proposed amendment restricting the government’s ability to dilute its stake had not been included in the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003. It also held that the doctrine of promissory estoppel could not be invoked to prevent the government from reducing its shareholding.

The judgment stated that there was no ambiguity in the Act and no provision that prohibited the government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI.

The doctrine of promissory estoppel generally concerns circumstances in which a promise or representation may be relied upon to prevent a party from going back on it. In this case, the court held that statements made during parliamentary proceedings on legislation could not be treated as a representation that restricted the government’s powers under the enacted law.

Union Budgets signal shift towards strategic disinvestment

The government also cited successive Union Budget speeches to underline the evolution of its policy towards IDBI Bank’s transformation and strategic disinvestment.

In the Union Budget for 2016–17, the then finance minister Arun Jaitley said the government would take forward the transformation of IDBI Bank and consider reducing its stake to below 50%.

The statement, made in paragraph 93 of the Budget speech, formed part of a broader agenda to strengthen public sector banks, operationalise the Bank Board Bureau and outline a roadmap for consolidation.

In the Union Budget for 2021–22, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman listed IDBI Bank among the transactions targeted for completion during the financial year as part of the government’s strategic disinvestment programme. The speech also referred to proposed privatisation initiatives involving other public sector banks and a general insurance company.

Government cites legislative and judicial record

The Centre said the legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, the Delhi High Court’s judgment and successive Budget speeches collectively demonstrate the evolution of its policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank.

It reiterated that the 2018 judgment clarified that parliamentary statements could not be used to restrict the government’s power to dilute its shareholding where the enacted legislation contained no such prohibition.

data.title: Reliance Jio IPO: From Dhirubhai Ambani's 1977 listing to Akash Ambani's mega issue - what's changed? Gen Z connect!
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Nearly five decades after Reliance Industries first made its debit in the Indian markets, the Ambani family is preparing for another landmark listing. Jio Platforms. The telecom and digital services business led by Akash Ambani, plans to raise around $3.2 billion through an initial public offering (IPO) and is opening on October 21.

The issue is set to test whether the Reliance name alone can attract investors in a market increasingly focused on valuations, profitability and future growth.

Jio's proposed IPO comes at a time when India's investor base has changed significantly. The country has more than 130 million registered stock-market investors, nearly 40% of whom are below 30, according to National Stock Exchange of India data.

Reliance's relationship with individual investors dates back to November 1977, when founder Dhirubhai Ambani raised Rs.2.8 crore through the company's first public offering. The issue attracted around 58,000 investors and was subscribed seven times, according to Reliance's annual report.

The listing helped popularise direct equity ownership among Indian households with Reliance's annual shareholder meetings eventually grew into mass gatherings.

Under Mukesh Ambani, Reliance evolved from a textiles and chemicals business into India's most valuable company, with interests spanning energy, consumer goods and telecommunications. Its telecom arm, Jio, transformed the sector after entering the market a decade ago with inexpensive 4G data services.

Unlike earlier generations, who often viewed Reliance as a long-term investment, younger investors are approaching the Jio IPO with a sharper focus on valuation, profitability and growth prospects. With Jio Platforms targeting a valuation of around $108 billion, the offering has sparked conversations among young investors about the company's digital ambitions, business model and potential listing gains.

In a post on X, young investor Sweta Chowdhury (@iSwetaChowdhury) said, "The Jio IPO offers an opportunity to examine the scale of India's digital economy and the business model behind one of its major players. Independent analysis matters."

Another young investor highlighted the importance of informed decision-making, stating, "The Jio IPO conversation reflects growing interest in India's digital businesses. Reliable information and balanced analysis should remain at the centre of the discussion. #JioIPO."

The interest is not limited to Jio's prominence or the possibility of listing-day gains. Some investors are also calculating the financial implications of the IPO's pricing and potential listing premium.

Young investor Sachya highlighted this aspect, saying, "Fun math: if Jio Platforms lists ~19% above the upper band, one lot moves from Rs.13,428 to ~ Rs.16,000. That Rs.2,500+ difference is exactly why this IPO is trending on every finance page."

Reliance shares have generated an annualised average return of around 29% since listing. However, the stock has fallen 23% this year amid a wider sell-off in Indian equities, putting it on course for its worst annual performance since 2011.

Meanwhile, it has shed 6.5% in 3 months, 10% in 6 months and 14% in the last 1 year.

The upcoming Jio listing is also a significant milestone for Akash Ambani, the 34-year-old managing director of Jio Platforms and Mukesh Ambani's eldest son. It marks his first major Reliance transaction undertaken independently.

As investors gear up for Reliance Industries' Rs.30,000 crore Jio Platforms IPO, Dalal Street is also evaluating what the mega issue could mean for other telecom stocks. Given the offering's scale, Jio's listing is expected to be a key near-term trigger for sector valuations, with investors watching how the market prices the telecom and digital services business against its listed peers.

Jio has reportedly attracted bids worth more than $20 billion, while overseas investors, including Fidelity Management & Research, Allianz SE and Capital Group, have indicated interest, according to people familiar with the matter.

The company has set a price band of Rs.1,065- Rs.1,119 per share, valuing it at around $108 billion at the upper end. This is below Bharti Airtel's market capitalisation of approximately $125 billion.

The Jio Platforms IPO was commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs.221 as of October 17, 2026. Based on the upper price band of Rs.1,119, this points to an estimated listing price of Rs.1,340 and a potential listing gain of 19.75%. However, the grey market is unofficial, and its premium does not guarantee the stock's listing price or subsequent performance.

The issue comprises a fresh offering of up to 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. Consequently, existing shareholders will not be selling their shares through the IPO. The revised issue size is nearly 14% lower than the approximately Rs.35,000 crore indicated in the draft papers.

Despite the reduction, the offering could overtake Hyundai Motor India's Rs.27,870 crore IPO in 2024 to become India's largest-ever public issue by value.

data.title: Who are Deepak Parekh and Paresh Sukthankar? Former HDFC and HDFC Bank execs Prem Watsa is consulting for IDBI Bank deal
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Fairfax Financial Holdings will acquire a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank for around Rs.53,000 crore ($5.5 billion), in what is poised to become the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank.

Fairfax will engage former HDFC Chairman Deepak Parekh and former HDFC Bank Deputy MD Paresh Sukthankar, as advisors to help it with its proposed acquisition, the Hindu BusinessLine reported on Friday, 16 October.

The deal was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), and the Canadian company will purchase the government's 30.48% stake (for about Rs.26,620 crore) and state-run Life Insurance Corporation of India's (LIC) 30.24% (for about Rs.26,440 crore), as per a PTI report.

Billionaire founder Prem Watsa expects that the new combined company will continue to be led by IDBI's current CEO and MD Rakesh Sharma, the HBL report said, adding that Fairfax has sorted out its leadership picks for the lender.

The executive suite will reportedly comprise former CSB Bank CEO CVR Rajendran, and NS Kannan, former MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Company MD and Chief Financial Officer of ICICI Bank. The report added that Kannan is set to take up the role of Chairman, subject to RBI approval.

Notably, the sale process for IDBI Bank began in 2022 and faced a setback earlier this year when initial bids fell below the government's reserve price. The deal is awaiting approval from the central bank, which will conduct a "fit and proper" assessment, and the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and other statutory authorities, the PTI report added.

Chairman of the erstwhile non-banking finance company HDFC, Deepak Parekh stepped down from his position in June 2023 after the merger of HDFC and HDFC Bank. He dubbed the merger as the biggest transaction in India's corporate history and the proposed entity will have combined assets of Rs.18 lakh crore.

Parekh joined his uncle's newly formed Housing Development and Finance Corporation in 1978 as an assistant general manager and turned the mortgage lender into a behemoth. He also spearheaded HDFC's entry into it with the creation of HDFC Bank.

Over the years, he also held positions as non-independent, non-executive chairman of HDFC Asset Management (a subsidiary of HDFC which runs HDFC Mutual Fund); non-executive chairman of HDFC ERGO General Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, Glaxo India Ltd, Burroughs Wellcome (India) Ltd, IDFC Ltd and GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd; and chairman of IDFC Private Equity Co Ltd.

Meanwhile, HDFC Bank's former Deputy MD Paresh Sukthankar resigned from the lender in August 2018 after a 24-year stint which began in 1994. He was promoted to the post from Executive Director role in March 2017. Analysts and watchers had credited the executive for "taking up the reins after Aditya Puri (then HDFC Bank CEO)", according to a report by the Financial Express.

data.title: Uniswap Slides Ahead Of CME Futures Debut As Binance Selling Pressure Eases
data.description:
Key points:
  • Uniswap dropped as selling pressure eased from its yearly high ahead of CME Group's futures debut on Monday.
  • UNI is still in a distribution phase, according to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost, although slowing Binance inflows could indicate a potential bottom.
  • In late September, Binance's inflows of UNI exceeded $40 million a day, and the Z-score rose above 4 several times.

Uniswap (UNI) fell on Saturday even as on-chain data showed selling pressure for UNI on Binance easing from its yearly high. The dip came two days before the token's futures debut on the CME Group (CME).

On Saturday, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said in an X post that UNI is in a distribution phase. That is a point at which holders move tokens to exchanges to sell. He said it was driven by rising exchange inflows.

The analyst pointed out that UNI inflows to Binance were the highest of the year in late September, topping $40 million a day. During that period, the Z-score rose above four several times. The Z-score shows how many standard deviations a data point is from the mean, and a value above four is considered an extreme outlier.

Inflows have stayed fairly active since then, but Darkfost noted that the momentum “seems to be fading.”

He said UNI could find a bottom if that slowdown persists. That would end the distribution phase that started when the token peaked at $10.9. Since then, UNI has fallen over 30% from that level, he said.

UNI’s price traded at about $7.33, down 1.4% over 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around UNI remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.

Strong Fundamentals Fueled Rally

Darkfost said the sell-off came after a strong run in Uniswap's fundamentals. He said total value locked (TVL), the value of assets deposited on the platform, exceeded $4 billion in September.

The decentralized exchange (DEX) volume reached an all-time high of $93.6 billion, according to the analyst. The token rallied as much as 370% from its June low, the analyst said.

DefiLlama data shows Uniswap's TVL at around $3.91 billion on Oct. 16. That was down from roughly $4.03 billion on Oct. 2.

CME Futures Set To Debut

In late September, CME Group said it would launch Uniswap futures on Oct. 19, pending regulatory review. Bitcoin Cash (BCH) futures are also set to launch the same day. A standard UNI contract will cover 10,000 tokens, while a micro contract will cover 1,000 tokens.

The exchange stated that crypto futures and options averaged 279,800 contracts a day in the first half of 2026, equivalent to $8.3 billion in notional value.

UNI is up 30% so far this year and 19% in the last 12 months.

Operating profit grew 6% YoY to Rs.11,083 crore, while core operating profit rose 11% to Rs.10,998 crore. Other income declined 1% to Rs.6,531 crore, even as fee income advanced 6% to Rs.6,381 crore.

Commenting on the bank's performance, managing director and CEO Amitabh Chaudhry said Axis Bank continued to focus on digital payments, secure banking, AI-driven innovation and strategic partnerships to strengthen its customer offerings.

Axis Bank reported a year-on-year improvement in its asset quality, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio falling 30 basis points (bps) to 1.16% in Q2FY27. The net non-performing asset (NNPA) ratio declined 9 bps to 0.35%.

Gross slippages dropped to Rs.4,762 crore during the September quarter, compared with Rs.5,566 crore in the preceding quarter and Rs.5,696 crore a year earlier. The net slippage ratio also declined 30 bps YoY to 0.75%.

The lender's annualised net credit cost came in at 0.45%, marking a reduction of 28 bps year-on-year and 18 bps sequentially. Meanwhile, its provision coverage ratio remained stable at 70%, unchanged from both the previous quarter and the corresponding period last year.

Axis Bank set aside Rs.1,694 crore towards provisions and contingencies in Q2FY27, including Rs.1,564 crore in specific loan-loss provisions.

As of September 30, 2026, the bank had accumulated Rs.15,860 crore in provisions against standard assets and additional provisions outside those for non-performing assets (NPAs). These were over and above the NPA provisions accounted for in the calculation of its provision coverage ratio.

Axis Bank's advances expanded 23% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.13.74 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026.

Retail lending increased 16% YoY to Rs.7.40 lakh crore, representing 54% of net advances. SME loans grew 25% to Rs.1.65 lakh crore, while corporate lending registered growth of 34%.

Total deposits rose 21% year-on-year and 6% sequentially to Rs.14.52 lakh crore on a month-end basis. Term deposits recorded 27% growth, while current account deposits increased 7% and savings account deposits advanced 12%.

The current account and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 36%. The bank's cost of funds also declined by 8 bps from the year-ago period.

Axis Bank's capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.27% as of September 30, 2026, while its common equity tier-1 (CET-1) ratio was 14.61%. The bank added 23 bps to its CET-1 ratio during the first half of FY27.

In addition, the lender held Rs.8,006 crore in provisions over and above those reflected in its reported capital adequacy ratio. These additional provisions represented a capital cushion equivalent to approximately 49 bps.

For the first half of FY27, Axis Bank's net profit climbed 30% year-on-year to Rs.14,117 crore from Rs.10,896 crore in H1FY26.

NII increased 10% to Rs.30,018 crore, while fee income rose 6% to Rs.12,536 crore. Operating profit advanced 4% to Rs.22,742 crore from Rs.21,928 crore in the year-ago period.

Core operating profit grew 11% to Rs.22,120 crore compared with Rs.20,010 crore in H1FY26.

Axis Bank shares ended Friday's session, October 16, at Rs.1,290, up 0.16%, ahead of the Q2FY27 earnings announcement.

The stock has gained around 4% over the past month but has declined 1.5% over three months and 4.5% over six months. Over the past year, it has advanced approximately 8%.

On a year-to-date basis, Axis Bank shares have gained 1.2%, outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 11.5% over the same period. The lender's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs.4.02 lakh crore.

data.title: Steve Eisman Warns OpenAI Is Now So Important That Its Collapse Could Cause A Recession In The US
data.description:
Key points:
  • Eisman said the scale of capital flowing into AI has made OpenAI much more important to the economy than many investors may realize.
  • He highlighted the capital expenditure commitments being made by cloud providers, chip companies and infrastructure firms to support the AI boom.
  • Eisman said that if demand for AI services suddenly weakened, the effects could ripple through the companies supplying that infrastructure.

“The Big Short” investor Steve Eisman is raising a fresh warning about the growing importance of artificial intelligence to the U.S. economy, arguing that OpenAI has become so deeply embedded in the AI investment boom that a collapse at the company could have consequences far beyond the technology sector.

Speaking on The Compound and Friends podcast on Friday, Eisman said the rapid growth of OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies has created an unusual concentration of economic and financial risk.

OpenAI Has Become ‘Systemically Important’

Eisman said the scale of capital flowing into AI has made OpenAI much more important to the economy than many investors may realize.

“If OpenAI went bankrupt tomorrow, and I'm not making that prediction, but let's just say that it did, I think the US economy would go into recession immediately,” Eisman warned.

He questioned how quickly an AI company could become so important to the broader economy.

Eisman highlighted the capital expenditure commitments being made by cloud providers, chip companies and infrastructure firms to support the AI boom. If demand for AI services suddenly weakened, the effects could ripple through the companies supplying that infrastructure, he explained.

AI Faces A Price War As ‘Token Maxing’ Ends

Eisman also sees a potential pressure point emerging inside the AI industry itself, which is falling prices.

He argued that the economics of the leading AI models are becoming increasingly difficult to sustain as cheaper open-weight models improve and customers begin scrutinizing their AI budgets.

“There's pretty good evidence that a price war is starting,” Eisman said.

He pointed to the rapid decline in the cost of running AI models and the emergence of open-weight alternatives as a major threat to companies trying to maintain premium pricing.

“You've got open weight models that are a tenth the price. They're not as good as the models, but you know, you don't need a Mercedes-Benz for every road trip,” he said.

Eisman believes the end of “token maxing”, which refers to companies spending aggressively on AI usage without closely scrutinizing the economics, could expose the industry's underlying vulnerabilities.

“They were making more money as a result of token maxing than they reasonably could have made on an ongoing basis once companies looked at their budgets and said, we obviously can't spend at this rate on AI as great as the technology is,” he said.

‘It’s All One Trade’, Says Eisman

For Eisman, the biggest concern extends beyond OpenAI itself. He sees the AI boom as increasingly interconnected, with major technology companies and infrastructure providers depending on continued AI spending.

“The problem with the AI story is a concentration problem,” Eisman said.

He specifically pointed to Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) customer concentration, arguing that the chipmaker’s exposure to a handful of major customers highlights how tightly connected the AI ecosystem has become.

But Eisman’s broader warning is about what happens to financial markets if the AI narrative changes. “There is only one narrative that matters right now, and that's AI,” he said. Eisman ultimately framed AI as the dominant trade driving markets, meaning a major reversal could have consequences well beyond individual AI companies.

“So, you tell me what happens to the AI narrative and I'll tell you what happens to the stock market,” he said. “It’s all one trade. It’s AI. Period. End of discussion.”

Eisman stressed that he is not predicting an OpenAI bankruptcy. He also said that while a major AI downturn could produce a bad recession, he does not view it as comparable to the 2008 financial crisis.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 0.26; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged lower by 0.27%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) fell 0.21%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) fell about 3.2% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) fell nearly 3%.

data.title: India's HDFC Bank Q2 profit rises 4.7%; deputy MD Bharucha to step down
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

India's largest private-sector lender, HDFC Bank , reported a second-quarter profit on Saturday that narrowly missed analyst expectations, as weaker treasury income and higher provisions for bad loans offset strong lending growth.

The lender also said in a regulatory filing that its deputy managing director Kaizad Bharucha will step down at the end of December.

The news comes days before a leadership change at the Mumbai-based lender. Anup Bagchi, a veteran of the ICICI group, takes over as managing director and CEO for three years from October 27, becoming HDFC Bank's first external chief executive.

Bharucha, who has been with HDFC Bank for over three decades, was one of two contenders for the top job, Reuters had reported.

Bagchi takes charge amid increased scrutiny of the bank's governance, profitability and operational performance.

The lender posted a standalone net profit of 195.10 billion Indian rupees ($2.05 billion) for the quarter ended September 30, compared with 186.41 billion rupees a year earlier.

Analysts had estimated a profit of 195.26 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Treasury trading gains fell to 7.8 billion rupees from 23.9 billion rupees a year earlier, weighing on earnings despite broad-based loan growth.

Other income, which includes gains on bonds and other investments, fell 3.6% to 138.31 billion rupees.

Indian lenders reported strong credit growth in the quarter across corporate and retail loans.

HDFC Bank's net interest income rose 9.7% to 346.19 billion rupees, with total loans up 16.3%. Deposits grew 18.8% from a year earlier, and the credit-to-deposit ratio stood at 96.0%.

Provisions for potential bad loans and other contingencies rose 2.1% to 35.74 billion rupees.

Asset quality improved. The gross non-performing asset ratio was 1.11% at the end of September, compared with 1.17% at the end of June.

($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

data.title: Circle Targets 40 New Markets As USDC Push Moves Beyond Crypto Trading
data.description:
TL;DR: Circle plans to expand USDC infrastructure into approximately 40 developing and emerging markets. The company is targeting international payments and access to digital dollars rather than relying solely on cryptocurrency exchange demand.

Circle is looking well beyond cryptocurrency trading as it prepares to extend USDC’s reach into approximately 40 emerging and developing markets.

CEO Jeremy Allaire outlined the ambition during discussions surrounding the October 16 international financial meetings in Bangkok. The strategy focuses on places where businesses and individuals want access to dollar-denominated payments but may face expensive or inefficient conventional banking arrangements.

The opportunity is straightforward: a stablecoin that can move between compatible wallets at any hour could offer a useful payment alternative. The difficult part is connecting those wallets to actual financial activity.

From Exchange Balances To Everyday Payments

USDC has long been widely used by cryptocurrency traders as a dollar-linked asset. Circle now wants to make it part of cross-border invoices, business settlement and consumer payments.

That requires more than issuing tokens. Businesses need reliable local currency conversion, banking connections, compliance arrangements and confidence that USDC can be redeemed as intended.

Circle has increasingly built partnerships around these services. Existing stablecoin initiatives, including creator payouts and digital payment programmes, show how digital dollars can be incorporated into familiar financial experiences.

Expansion Will Be Uneven

Regulation is likely to determine the pace of Circle’s international push. Some countries welcome stablecoin payment infrastructure, while others restrict foreign currency access or require substantial local licensing.

Tether’s USDT is also already entrenched across a number of international markets.

Circle must therefore establish the practical value of USDC for customers who may never buy Bitcoin or speculate on another cryptocurrency. If the strategy succeeds, its next stage of growth could depend less on crypto market cycles and more on the ordinary movement of money.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Polymarket sees 31% chance of S&P 500 hitting 8,000 by year-end
data.description:
Prediction market Polymarket puts the probability of the S&P 500 crossing 8,000 by the end of 2026 at 31%. The benchmark closed at 7,659.44 on Friday, October 16, after gaining nearly 2% for the week despite a sell-off in technology and semiconductor stocks. A move to 8,000 would require a gain of around 4.4% from Friday’s close.

The S&P 500’s earnings outlook remains a key pillar of the bull market. According to FactSet, Q3 earnings are projected to grow 29% year-on-year, while full-year 2026 earnings growth is forecast at 32.8%. Revenue growth for the third quarter is estimated at 12.6%.

Just 9% of S&P 500 companies had reported their third-quarter results as of the latest available data. Of those, 84% beat earnings per share (EPS) estimates, above the five-year average of 78%. However, the aggregate earnings surprise was only 2.6%, well below the five-year average of 7.5%.

That makes the coming weeks crucial: investors will look for evidence that earnings strength extends beyond a handful of large companies and that AI investments are translating into sustainable profits.

Oil, yields and AI concerns threaten the rally

The biggest challenge for equities remains the combination of higher energy prices and persistent inflationary pressure. Brent crude climbed to $110 a barrel on Friday for the first time since May, as escalating Middle East tensions, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and fresh concerns over Russian energy supplies heightened fears of further disruptions.

Investors are also reassessing the sustainability of the AI-driven rally, with concerns over spending, financing and returns on heavy AI investments weighing on chipmakers and technology stocks.

In its latest GREED & fear note, Jefferies warned that global AI stocks’ earnings growth is expected to slow sharply over the next two years, urging investors to look beyond the AI trade for opportunities.

Read More: Jefferies warns AI earnings growth to slow sharply in next 2 years, urges investors to diversify

In a report titled “Diversifying Beyond AI”, Jefferies said consensus earnings growth for AI-related stocks in the MSCI AC World Index is projected to decline from around 100% in 2026 to 30% in 2027 and moderate further to 22% in 2028.

Fed policy remains crucial

Investors have pared back bets on a rate hike at the Federal Reserve’s October 27–28 policy meeting. Comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the International Monetary Fund’s annual meeting did not dislodge expectations that rates will remain unchanged at the end of the month.

The Fed’s next move, the trajectory of crude prices and the ability of corporate earnings to meet elevated expectations will be key factors in determining whether the S&P 500 can advance towards 8,000 before the year ends.

data.title: HDFC Bank's Kaizad Bharucha to exit on December 31 after over three decades
data.description:
HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has sought to step down from the bank’s service with effect from the close of business hours on December 31, 2026, the lender said in a stock exchange filing on Saturday, October 17.

The bank’s Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee (GNRC), at its meeting on October 16, and the board of directors, at its meeting on October 17, accepted Bharucha’s request, which will be forwarded to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for approval.

The bank said the committee and board placed on record their appreciation for Bharucha’s contribution over an association spanning more than three decades. It particularly acknowledged his role in conceptualising, establishing and developing the bank’s credit architecture, which it described as one of its defining institutional strengths.

Bharucha joined HDFC Bank in October 1995 and became Deputy Managing Director in April 2023. He has been responsible for several businesses, including retail assets, rural banking, small and medium enterprises, emerging corporates and corporate banking.

Bharucha's exit follows HDFC Bank CEO succession race

Bharucha’s exit comes after he emerged as a leading internal contender to succeed Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is due to step down at the end of his term on October 26, 2026.

Media reports in August and September said HDFC Bank had considered Bharucha alongside an external candidate for the top job. The bank subsequently confirmed that it had submitted two names to the RBI but did not disclose the candidates’ identities.

Bharucha joined the bank’s board in 2014 and is its longest-serving executive board member, according to the bank’s website. Reports had also noted that regulatory tenure limits could affect his eligibility for a full three-year term as chief executive.

The company did not state the reason for Bharucha’s decision to leave or disclose the identity of the candidates submitted to the RBI.
